title: Awesome
body:
This is an excellent habit tracker. One thing to note is that nearly all trackers allow you to select a good or bad habit but not to simply track a habit. This is one of the only ones I found that allowed you to create a habit and then track it without having to be forced to set a goal number.

In fact the way this can be used to track all sorts of things like exercise, sleep ect. I think the developers realise this due to the apple health integration but ultimately this app may be more valuable in its ability to track things generally as opposed to habits specifically. For example, if they allowed custom measurement units to be add you could set up a ‘habit’ with things like your vo2max or other vitals. There is a hole in the market for just a general flexible tracking app that you put health data in. Basic blood test could be logged in a format like this too.

Lots of potential for this app if they push it into a general tracker.

title: Ótimo app para hábitos — só falta funcionar no Apple Watch
body:
Gostei muito do app! Experimentei o teste gratuito da versão paga e realmente é muito útil. Ele oferece opções de pagamento mensal, anual e vitalícia, o que dá flexibilidade para escolher o que cabe melhor no bolso. O app é super intuitivo e fácil de usar — com um pouco de tempo e criatividade, dá pra criar várias formas interessantes de acompanhar seus hábitos. Além disso, a análise que ele fornece sobre o seu desempenho é bem completa. Se você gosta de acompanhar sua evolução e criar rotinas mais conscientes, pode ser uma ótima escolha!

O único ponto negativo é que na App Store aparece uma imagem indicando suporte para o Apple Watch, mas infelizmente não consegui baixar o app no relógio. Seria ótimo se essa integração funcionasse ou se fosse melhor esclarecida na descrição.

body:
*23/Nov/24 update

As a replacement of another app I used to use for this purpose, I am trying to use Grit to track and remind me of the medicine pills I need to take on a daily basis.

What I am missing now is a feature to have a recurring notification that will appear from time to time (configurable e.g. every 15mins) and that will only stop showing up if I mark the habit as done.

Another useful feature would be to set the deadline time within the day that a habit must be completed by. That would allow the badge number to only show the pending habits at a given time instead of all the habits pending on that day.

Can you consider adding these feature in future releases, please?

*Comments from my previous updates 

I have been testing many habit tracking apps in the last couple of months and several ones on a daily basis in the last week. This is the one I have chosen so I have just subscribed to the premium version. Elegant UI, full of features and customization options. Keep up the great work, Stephan.

title: A Fresh Take on Habit Tracking
body:
As an early adopter of the iPhone and a frequent user of the App Store, I've explored countless habit tracking apps over the years. Despite already having a lifetime habit app that I use regularly, the design of Grit immediately caught my eye. Initially, I wasn't looking for another habit app, as I was already using two simultaneously.

However, something about Grit intrigued me. After testing the app and interacting with the developer, who was both responsive and helpful, I found myself integrating Grit into my daily routine. The attention to detail, along with its impressive visuals and user-friendly interface, made it clear that it was crafted by someone who not only cares deeply about their work but also uses the app themselves.

Following my trial period, I've decided to pay for Grit without any hesitation. I'm grateful for developers who still dedicate so much effort to the quality and functionality of their apps.

Ich Nutze die App sowohl für private, als auch für mein Unternehmen. 

Dank der App kann ich meine Gewohnheiten nicht nur besser steuern, sondern auch feste in meinen Alltag integrieren und somit auch das Risiko minimieren wichtige to-dos nicht zu erledigen. 

Mittlerweile nutzen auch die meisten meiner Freunde die App und es erleichtert wirklich vielen. 

Normalerweise vergisst man ja die banalsten Dinge, wie z.B. ein Glas Wasser auf nüchternen Magen trinken o.ä. aber dank der App habe ich es geschafft meine Routinen wirklich durchzuziehen.

No permite un full check a no ser que sea 1 count. No sincroniza bien mi apple watch. No es intuitivo el añadir vacaciones. No permite usar timers desde Apple Watch, ni pasar entre dias. Los widget no son visuales si esta completo o no el hábito dependiento del color…

Esta app solventa todo esto, y es todo lo que andaba buscando. Pagaré el precio completo para apoyarla. Y a pesar de que no hay versión gratuita lo merece, las cosas que tienen alto valor cuestan dinero.

La única queja: en el apple watch me gustaría tener el mismo quick check que hay en la app móvil para poder hacer check sin acceder al hábito. Y quizas una mejora del diseño de la página de inicio. Con esto ya sería un 10/10.

title: Almost perfect
body:
Grit has frankly astonished me, as someone who has downloaded hundreds of planner and todo apps, but never actually stuck with one. It is very easy and quick to add your habits and tasks. There are a good number of different tracking inputs too; I particularly appreciate the built in timers. I also love how you can enter in one time tasks much more easily and efficiently than in many other habit trackers. I never understood why anyone would want a separate app JUST for repeating tasks but that might just be me. There are two small changes that would make the app perfect for me. The first would be a setting whereby the tasks/habits that you create automatically adopt the colour and icon from their primary “group”, so I would no longer have to manually make everything match. Secondly, a system of tags, similar to the way groups work, would be useful for categorisation, enabling me to group a habit as “personal” but also tag it as “health” related, without it appearing twice on the dashboard/task list. In other words, a user would then be able to categorise a habit or task by its type (habit, bad habit, one off task) using the groups feature and have it appear as that in the dashboard, but also be able to describe it by its actual function or purpose as well through use of individual user created ‘tags’.

I really appreciate the app, and while I’m sure that there are probably bigger issues and lots of bugs that need fixing before adding any additional features, I really hope you take on my feedback!

title: Awesome app and outstanding support!
body:
I’ve been using Grit for barely a couple of weeks, but I can happily say I will be using it long-term. 

I recently started needing to log medication multiple times a day, along with wanting to track some other regular habits. I must have tried nearly two dozen apps and not a single one did everything I wanted, including this one. However, I put in a couple of feature requests and the developer, Stephan, implemented them in less than 24hrs. I have since made some more complex requests and these have been added too! 

The app itself is a joy to use. At first glance, it may seem quite simple, but everything that’s needed is there with no unnecessary clutter. It’s very easy to add positive and negative habits with varying frequencies. You can also add habits without a goal, great if you simply want to track something. 

The main statistics screen for each habit is very clean. It’s easy to see progress (and failures!) on the colourful calendar and there is an info box which highlights key data. My favourite section is the performance charts - these show your stats for selectable time periods, both as a total figure and a percentage. What I love is that you can clearly see when you’ve exceeded a habit goal as well as just achieving it. Very motivational!

I am very happy to have found this little app. It’s pretty much perfect for my needs now. I would perhaps like to see the Watch app fleshed out a bit more and the option to customise the widgets, but that’s nitpicking and I’m sure Stephan has plenty of ideas for the future. :)

title: Красивое и вкусное
body:
Я перепробовала много трекеров привычек, но Grit зацепил меня сильнее всего, так что в благодарность разработчику я купила lifetime версию.

Приложение очень красивое, им приятно пользоваться, оно не перегружено лишними деталями, мне хочется заходить сюда снова и снова и отмечать свои привычки. На мой взгляд, такие ощущения - это самое важное в трекере привычек, потому что именно они не позволяют забросить приложение через неделю, как это получилось у меня с Habitica - красивым, интересным, но переусложненным трекером, который со временем превратился для меня в работу. Я не хочу сказать, что Habitica плохая, но для такого рассеянного человека с СДВГ как я, разноцветный и вкусненький Grit оказался полезнее и приятнее.

Минусы/пожелания:
1. Хотелось бы увидеть более минималистичный heatmap виджет - без лишних подписей и месяцев. Только название привычки и растянутый на весь виджет heatmap с разноцветными квадратиками, как это сделано в Ripples и Habitkit.
2. В разделе "Статистика" много лишнего и мало полезного. Для мотивации и отслеживания успехов достаточно одного календарика с heatmap и процентом успеха, остальная часть статистики должна быть направлена на понимание того, почему я не выполнила свои привычки. Можно сделать это через трекер настроения (в виде смайликов, на которые можно нажимать каждый день), уровня энергии (в виде батарейки) или кнопки "Почему не получилось" с вариантами ответа, которые бы учитывались в статистике.

“1/185 lbs, 170lbs”

instead of

title: Great, though Watch app is limited
body:
This app is great for shift workers and people who stay up late. You can set the time that the day starts, so your habits don’t fail at midnight like so many other apps do. 

One critique/feature request is that the Apple Watch side of this is really lacking customizability. title: Nearly Perfect…
body:
I’ve been using Grit for a short time, and it has quickly become one of my favorite productivity tools. The app’s design is sleek, intuitive, and highly customizable, making it easy to track habits and stay on top of my goals. I especially love the ability to set specific goals and track progress over time—it’s a game-changer for habit-building.

However, the one area where Grit falls just short of perfection is the lack of support for non-repeatable, one-time tasks. While the app excels at habit tracking, it would be incredibly useful to have the ability to add one-off tasks that don’t factor into the overall habit metrics. This functionality would consolidate all my to-do items into one app and eliminate the need for other tools like Apple’s Notes.

This minor shortcoming is the only thing keeping Grit from being a perfect five-star, daily-use application for me. With the addition of non-repeatable tasks, this app would truly be unbeatable.

Despite this, I can’t recommend Grit enough—it’s a fantastic tool for anyone looking to take control of their habits and achieve their goals. Here’s hoping this already great app continues to get even better!

Rating: ★★★★☆

title: Almost perfect! Minor fix needed
body:
This is the perfect app to keep an adhd individual on track. I love that I can set goals for different parts of the day and categorize them as well as location based goals. The color coding that can be personalized is extremely helpful, as well. The habit tracker with graph charts are helpful to see trends, I like this feature even as someone I would not consider “math minded.” I’ve tried many habit tracking apps and while each has its perks, this is the one I’ve returned to and actually deemed worth the year investment, and then some. This app is easily worth more than they ask for! My one and only complaint is that it lacks the ability to set goals for specific days, and not others. Other reviews have mentioned this con, and I agree. I wish to set specific days for things such as the gym or a specific household chore, work task etc. If this ability is added in future updates I shall amend my review to state that this is absolute perfection.

Edit: yes you can set a weekly habit but you’re unable to select the specific day, it stays in your list of tasks to do until you “check” it off and that’s defeating the purpose of trying to check off everything in one day. Having the ability to mark a specific task to show up on the list only on Mondays or Tuesdays would be absolutely helpful!
